claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a high-temperature BCC state.
Phase stability in this alloy is governed by competition between thermodynamic and kinetic factors.
High-throughput first-principles calculations can predict this competition and the resulting phase stability.
The proposed calculations vary temperature from 1000 to 1500 K and vary the concentration of each element by ±2%.
Formation of coherent precipitates is a structural mediator of phase stability.
Grain boundaries are a structural mediator of phase stability.
Thermodynamic instability is driven by composition-dependent changes in free energy.
Diffusion rates influence the phase stability or transformation behavior.
Nucleation barriers influence the phase stability or transformation behavior.
The proposed variation will produce a 15% increase in phase stability relative to Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 at 1200 K with no composition variation.
A reduction in precipitate formation is a measure of increased phase stability.
The hypothesis applies over 1000–1500 K and composition variations of ±5% for each element.
Impurities and defects are neglected by the proposed model.
Neglecting impurities and defects may limit prediction accuracy.

contradictions.description: The test conditions specify ±2% variation of each element, whereas the stated boundary specifies ±5%, without distinguishing the tested range from the claimed applicability range.
